content: Business invariants and history belong to one named bounded context. Contexts integrate through stable IDs and published contracts; desktop, web, and KiCad-facing shells stay thin composition roots. Avoid ownership-free core, models, or utils modules.

title: Keep SQLite roles physically and logically separate
rationale: The team-authoritative database, each desktop replica, generated KiCad projection, and external read-only databases serve different consistency and authority roles. Synchronize records and regenerate projections atomically; never multi-writer-sync SQLite files.

title: Use PocketBase as the sole team backend
rationale: PocketBase is selected for its maturity, documentation, authentication, realtime, file, migration, hook, job, and backup capabilities. Domain rules remain in application-owned interfaces and protected server-side commands, but the repository will not build an alternate-provider adapter or comparison harness. Pin every PocketBase version and checksum, rehearse upgrades, preserve a canonical export, and prove blank-environment recovery.

content: Every frontend seed owns its full autonomous feedback loop: add semantic and accessibility assertions, automate the critical browser or native Tauri journey, capture deterministic screenshots for materially distinct states, inspect actual and diff images, record a concise visual critique, correct every material issue, and rerun. Screenshot review complements behavior tests; baseline changes are explicit and never self-accepted merely because a test changed.

name: Restore PocketBase through an S3-compatible blank-environment drill
description: Use isolated MinIO buckets to test PocketBase backup upload and recovery. Seed records and files, create and checksum the backup, destroy disposable PocketBase state, restore into a blank pinned instance, and compare records, files, hashes, rules, migrations, and version manifest. PocketBase pb_data backups exclude files stored in S3, so any S3-backed application objects require their own replication and restore proof. MinIO proves S3 protocol behavior, not AWS-specific IAM, KMS, TLS, region, or lifecycle configuration.

outcomes.test_results: 16 Rust tests, fmt, clippy -D warnings, manifest check, and source-immutability gate passed; independent review PASS

name: Loss-detecting fixture boundaries fail closed
description: Repository fixture and import oracles classify serialized path syntax lexically rather than with host OS path semantics; accept only exact-case, root-contained regular files; reject traversal and links/reparse points before probing; propagate discovery failures; preserve SQLite NULL distinctly from empty text; and report field-level semantic differences alongside byte identity.

title: Develop and validate natively on Windows for now; defer the Docker lab
rationale: The user chose Windows-native work for the time being so Docker is not a dependency. The Rust workspace gate (cargo test, fmt, clippy -D warnings, the import fixture check) must pass on Windows. The Docker AFK lab stays in the repo but isn't run or extended until kicad-parts-c748 resumes it.

description: On Windows, core.autocrlf=true rewrote LF catalog files to CRLF on checkout. The import oracle had recorded byte hashes from one such mixed checkout, so it failed on any other checkout and on Linux. A lock test that matched on newline also failed.
resolution: .gitattributes sets '* text=auto eol=lf' and '-text' on database/, symbols/, footprints/, 3d-models/ and design-blocks/, so the working tree equals the committed bytes on every OS. The manifest's byte hashes now describe the committed bytes; only byte fields changed and every semantic hash still matched. database/parts.sqlite is committed as a frozen projection. Tests that change serialization flip the line ending instead of assuming CRLF.

content: Guard execution environments with exhaustive allowlists, not word filters. Examples: the normalized Compose policy, per-image Dockerfile contracts (bases, downloads, checksums, apt packages, RUN programs), and a single Program enum enforced by clippy disallowed-methods on Command::new. Word bans had to obfuscate their own source and still let unlisted tools through.

title: KiCad 10 is a required dependency that the app, tests, and CI may run
rationale: The product serves people who already have KiCad installed, and CI runners will have it too. Use the installed KiCad, mainly kicad-cli, wherever it already does the job instead of reimplementing it. Validate against a real KiCad 10 in automated tests, and keep a manual checklist only for behaviour kicad-cli cannot show. KiCad safety rules still apply: never modify an open design or editable library behind KiCad (mx-3903cc, mx-70700f).

description: tauri-driver forwards tauri:options.args to msedgedriver, which treats them as browser switches: it sorts them, lowercases them, and turns a standalone value into its own --switch, so '--data-dir C:\x' reaches the app as '--c:\x --data-dir'.
resolution: Launch options the desktop journeys pass must use the --name=value form; apps/desktop parses both forms and ignores unknown arguments.

title: Hold Leptos at 0.8.3 while the toolchain is Rust 1.85
rationale: Leptos 0.8.4+ declares rust-version 1.88, and its sub-crates (server_fn_macro, server_fn_macro_default) publish no rust-version, so the fallback resolver picks releases built on syn 3 that break leptos_macro 0.8.3. apps/desktop-ui/Cargo.toml pins leptos, server_fn_macro and server_fn_macro_default to =0.8.3 (and Cargo.lock follows); revisit when the toolchain moves to 1.88+.

name: Run desktop journeys on a hidden Win32 desktop
description: tooling/journey-desktop creates a run-scoped desktop with CreateDesktopW (desktop rights only: create window/menu, read/write objects, enumerate) and starts tauri-driver on it with CreateProcessW (STARTUPINFOW.lpDesktop = winsta0\<name>), inside a kill-on-close job. msedgedriver, the Tauri app and WebView2 inherit the desktop, so journeys show no window and take no focus. The helper also waits on its parent (the Node runner) and kills the job if the runner dies, even by taskkill /F; the runner refuses to start if the driver port is taken. WebView2 still renders: all screenshots matched a visible run pixel for pixel except for random temp paths and mouse hover (worst 2.1% of pixels), with no extra WebView2 flags; run time was the same (18.3 s hidden vs 18.4 s visible). npm run journeys is hidden by default; --visible or JOURNEYS_VISIBLE=1 uses the real desktop.
pocketbase serve on a data directory with no superuser opens its installer page in the user's default browser (a pop-up on the developer's laptop during tests).
resolution: tooling/native-services: PocketBaseServer::start takes a Superuser and always runs 'pocketbase superuser upsert' first (blank, restored and upgraded instances alike); service processes start suspended in a kill-on-close job with ActiveProcessLimit=1 so they cannot launch any child (browser); a log containing the installer banner fails the start.

description: Rust's Path::canonicalize on Windows returns a verbatim \?\C:\... path; Go reads the '?' as a glob wildcard, so go:embed patterns matched nothing and the MinIO build failed with 'pattern ...: no matching files found'.
resolution: native_services::repository_root strips the \?\ prefix (not \?\UNC\) before paths are handed to child programs.

name: Native disposable PocketBase and MinIO for tests
description: tooling/native-services reads infra/versions.lock (the Docker lab's typed lock, which also pins the Windows assets and the minio.exe SHA-256), caches checksum-verified downloads and the MinIO source build under target/native-services, and runs services on random 127.0.0.1 ports with per-run credentials, CREATE_NO_WINDOW and a kill-on-close single-process job. The MinIO build is only reproducible with -buildvcs=false: the source is unpacked inside this repository's target/, so Go otherwise stamps the kicad-parts commit and dirty flag (vcs.revision/vcs.modified) into the binary and the pinned hash only matches one commit. The build also runs with a cleared environment (no PATH, GOENV=off, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, CGO_ENABLED=0, fixed GOOS/GOARCH/GOAMD64, -trimpath); prove a re-pin with cold builds in fresh clones outside the repository. PocketBase 0.38 refuses its in-place backup restore on Windows ('restore is not supported on Windows', 204 then a logged error), so recovery downloads the backup from S3 and unpacks it into an empty pb_data. MinIO needs /minio/health/ready (not /live) before bucket calls.

content: Mulch decision records are the only decision log. Don't create docs/adr/. When the domain-modeling skill would offer an ADR (the decision is hard to reverse, surprising, and a real trade-off), record a mulch decision instead, so there is one source of truth. Decided by the user on 2026-10-08.

description: In a PocketBase JSVM route, JSON.stringify(e.requestInfo().body) is not deterministic: the parsed body is a Go map whose key order varies per request, so a request hash built from it made an identical retry look like a reused correlation ID (409).
resolution: Build request hashes from validated values in a fixed order, e.g. JSON.stringify([reason, sources.map(...), parts.map(...)]) as catalog_csv_imports.pb.js and collab_commands.pb.js do.

description: pocketbase migrate down asks 'Do you really want to revert...? (y/N)'; with stdin closed (run_hidden) it prints 'The command has been cancelled' and still exits 0, so a test that checks only the exit status passes without reverting anything.
resolution: native_services::run_hidden_with_input writes 'y\n' to stdin (still windowless, in the kill-on-close job); assert stdout contains 'Reverted <migration>' and inspect data.db (see tooling/catalog-import test the_catalog_migration_rolls_back_from_a_populated_instance).

content: Keep terminology as simple as possible for people. Use plain, everyday words and the fewest terms in the glossaries, code names, docs and UI, following the ISO 24495 plain-language skills (iso-24495-1 for text, iso-24495-code for code). When a new concept needs a name, prefer a plain phrase over a new coined term. The user asked for this on 2026-10-09.

description: In a PocketBase 0.38 JSVM onRecordUpdate hook, e.record.original() is empty for a record that the same handler created and then saved again (the CSV import creates a part, then sets its current revision), so a guard comparing fields with original() refused the import.
resolution: Read the stored row inside the hook with e.app.findRecordById(collection, e.record.id); e.app is the transaction, so it sees rows written earlier in the same transaction (see infra/pocketbase/pb_hooks/catalog_write_guards.pb.js).

description: PocketBase capitalises the first letter of an ApiError message and adds a full stop, so BadRequestError(`${reference} is not ...`) reached the user as 'G-pas:NOPE is not ...'. In migrations, collection.updateRule is a Go string pointer: typeof is not 'string', so string checks on it silently fail.
resolution: Start route error messages with a plain word ('the symbol g-pas:NOPE is not in the Catalog'). Convert rules with String(rule) before comparing or slicing (1791600000_catalog_edits.js down migration).

description: Under tauri-driver, msedgedriver launches the app with its own WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS (remote debugging and automation switches), replacing any value the runner set, and tauri:options.args reach only the app's command line. So neither --force-device-scale-factor in tauri:options.args nor in the runner's environment changed WebView2's scale; at 150% display scaling screenshots stayed 1920x1200. Forcing the scale alone also made the CSS viewport 1920x1200, because the window is sized in logical pixels.
resolution: apps/desktop takes --display-scale=N (Windows only): before Tauri starts it appends --force-device-scale-factor=N to WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS, and in setup it sizes the window (and its minimum) in screen pixels (configured size x N). The journeys pass --display-scale=1 and assert devicePixelRatio 1 and 1280x800 PNGs.

name: Journey screenshots are compared with reviewed baselines, and incomplete contrast checks are re-run
description: apps/desktop/journeys/baselines holds one reviewed PNG per screenshot state. harness.mjs compares each screenshot with pixelmatch (threshold 0.1, anti-aliasing ignored) and fails above 20 different pixels (repeated runs differ by 0-2; one character is 30-80); diffs go to target/journeys/latest/diffs and visual-summary.json. Missing, changed or unused baselines fail with a plain message; only npm run journeys -- --update-baselines writes them. Keep screenshots deterministic first: fixed temp folder names under <temp>/kicad-parts-journeys, waits for async states (results list after a restore, live-updates badge), and hide only text that must vary: <time> elements always, other selectors via screenshot(..., { hide }) (hatched with CSSOM, since the CSP blocks inline styles). axe marks colour contrast incomplete for rows clipped by a scrolled list (elmPartiallyObscured) or text under an open menu (bgOverlap); assertAccessible re-runs color-contrast on each such element scrolled into view with covering elements made invisible, restores the page, and fails on a violation or a check still incomplete.
